title: Ethiopia's Big Election: 50 Million Voters, 47 Parties, and One Big Choice
summary: Imagine a country where half the population is under 19 years old. That's Ethiopia! On Monday, millions of young people — and their parents — will vote in a huge election. Over 50 million voters are registered. They'll pick from 47 political parties and more than 10,900 candidates. The winners will form the parliament, and then choose the prime minister. The current prime minister is Abiy Ahmed. His party, the Prosperity Party, wants to keep power. It focuses on national unity and economic growth. Other big parties include the National Movement of Amhara (NAMA), which fights for the Amhara region's rights, and the Ethiopian Citizens for Social Justice (EZEMA), which wants more democracy and free markets. There's also a coalition called Peace for Ethiopia, made of smaller regional parties. Many candidates are running for regional councils too. Women make up about half of all voters. With so many young people, this election could shape Ethiopia's future for decades. The results will show which direction the country wants to go.
why_it_matters: When a country has many young people, elections like this decide the kind of schools, jobs, and communities they will grow up with, showing that even though you're young, your nation's future includes you.
